summary: Improvement cycle addressing external reviewer (berendt) feedback on CC-0084. Changes: (1) extended TestValidateCreate_RunsAllValidations to break 5 new CC-0084 axes — graceful termination, uWSGI drain, keep-alive, strategy — with substring assertions for terminationGracePeriodSeconds, preStopSleepSeconds, harakiri, httpKeepAliveTimeout, and strategy so future short-circuit regressions are caught (W-001); (2) removed local ptrInt32/ptrInt64 helpers and migrated 27 call sites to k8s.io/utils/ptr.To (W-002); (3) deploymentStrategy() now returns *keystone.Spec.Strategy.DeepCopy() on the override path with a rewritten docstring that accurately describes aliasing guarantees (W-003); (4) chainsaw load-gen Job is pre-deleted with --ignore-not-found --wait=true before apply so rapid CI retries don't race the 300s TTL (I-001); (5) added discoverability link from docs/reference/keystone-crd.md to the published architecture site (I-002). All unit tests pass, go vet clean, build clean.

Aggregate webhook test now covers all new CC-0084 validation paths
Go build succeeds across operator module
Edge cases covered: deep-copy verified, pre-delete idempotent, nil-grace/preStop default resolution

No duplicated pointer helpers — all call sites use the standard generic helper
Chainsaw cleanup matches the CC-0048 pattern referenced in tests/e2e-chaos/cronjob-rotation-failure/

security_checklist.item: No new attack surface introduced; changes are test-only, docstring, and a defensive DeepCopy
No secrets or sensitive data touched

No scope creep; every change maps to a specific berendt finding

next_steps: Merge after CI green; the architecture submodule (7cfe7d2) should be verified by a reviewer with that repo cloned per the original I-002 note, but the improvement cycle has addressed the discoverability gap via the new cross-repo link in docs/reference/keystone-crd.md.
